newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Cautious Irish bonds slip, track overseas weakness.
newsitem.headline: Cautious Irish bonds slip, track overseas weakness.

text.p: Irish bonds slipped, tracking weak international markets on Wednesday, with bunds sharply down after a raft of economic data and rumours of an EMU delay, weighed on performance, dealers said.

''We're seeing some very weak conditions here today,'' Padhraic Garvey, economist with Riada stockbrokers said. ''The backdrop isn't great - firstly, on the currency market the punt is down against the mark, and secondly, we're hearing remarks this afternoon from Waigel suggesting there may be a questionmark over whether EMU will go ahead on time or not.''

By 1700 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down almost 31 pence from Tuesday's close at 102.25 to yield 5.91 percent while the benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 fell 65 pence from the close at 109.65 to yield 6.58 percent.

Spooked bond markets tumbled as German finance minister Theo Waigel increased worries over the timetable for EMU. Speaking to reporters after a meeting, Waigel said the timetable for monetary union was not as important as fulfilling the fiscal goals.

Garvey said Irish bonds were underperforming bunds by between five and seven basis points in shorts and by between one and two basis points further up the curve. ''We're performing equally as badly as Germany in the 10-year bond,'' he said.

He said he doubted the fall in Europe today was due to anticipation of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's economic report to Congress, due 1900 GMT: ''I haven't heard a good reason except for a feeling of uncertainty - over EMU and a direction for the bunds market. I think we're in quite a volatile environment at the moment with bund markets looking for a direction.''
Elsewhere, UK gilts were under pressure, following nervous bunds downward to end three-quarters of a point lower on the session.
